Annapurna conservation area is the first and largest protected area of Nepal.
It is rich in biodiversity and is home for 1,226 species of flowering plants, 105 mammals, 518 birds, 40 reptiles and 23 amphibians.
It comprises the Annapurna himalayan range and Kali Gandaki River Valley (the world's deepest valley).
